\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{અત્યંત} (atyant)}{અત્યંત (atyant)}]{\gu{અત્યંત} (atyant) — extremely}

\label{lesson:GU-C379-atyant}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a proportion, then the Gujarati for to tolerate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{અત્યંત}}
\textbf{\gu{અત્યંત}} — \emph{atyant} — \textquotedblleft{}extremely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તમે} \gu{બપોરે} \gu{ચાલશો} \gu{તો} \gu{તમને} \gu{અત્યંત} \gu{થાક} \gu{લાગશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tame bapore cālśo to tamne atyant thāk lāgśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you walk in the midday heat, you will be extremely tired.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{અત્યંત}} (\emph{atyant}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{atyanta}, \textquotedblleft{}beyond the proper end or limit\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atyant}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atyant}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tame bapore cālśo to tamne atyant thāk lāgśe.} — If you walk in the midday heat, you will be extremely tired.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a proportion, then the Gujarati for to tolerate, then say \emph{atyant} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{અત્યંત} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Extremely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સાવ} (sāv)}{સાવ (sāv)}]{\gu{સાવ} (sāv) — utterly}

\label{lesson:GU-C379-sav}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to tolerate, then the Gujarati for extremely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સાવ}}
\textbf{\gu{સાવ}} — \emph{sāv} — \textquotedblleft{}utterly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તમે} \gu{આ} \gu{દવા} \gu{લેશો} \gu{તો} \gu{દુખાવો} \gu{સાવ} \gu{મટી} \gu{જશે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tame ā davā leśo to dukhāvo sāv maṭī jaśe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you take this medicine, the pain will go away completely.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સાવ}} (\emph{sāv}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{sárva}, \textquotedblleft{}all, whole\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Gujarati \emph{sāv}, \textquotedblleft{}wholly\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13276).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāv}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāv}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tame ā davā leśo to dukhāvo sāv maṭī jaśe.} — If you take this medicine, the pain will go away completely.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to tolerate, then the Gujarati for extremely, then say \emph{sāv} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{સાવ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Utterly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સંપૂર્ણ} (sampūrṇ)}{સંપૂર્ણ (sampūrṇ)}]{\gu{સંપૂર્ણ} (sampūrṇ) — complete}

\label{lesson:GU-C379-sampurn}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for extremely, then the Gujarati for utterly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સંપૂર્ણ}}
\textbf{\gu{સંપૂર્ણ}} — \emph{sampūrṇ} — \textquotedblleft{}complete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{કામ} \gu{સંપૂર્ણ} \gu{થશે} \gu{તો} \gu{અમે} \gu{પગાર} \gu{ચૂકવીશું}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo kām sampūrṇ thaśe to ame pagār cūkvīśũ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the work is completed, we will pay the wages.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સંપૂર્ણ}} (\emph{sampūrṇ}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{sampūrṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}completely filled, full\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sampūrṇ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo kām sampūrṇ thaśe to ame pagār cūkvīśũ.} — If the work is completed, we will pay the wages.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for extremely, then the Gujarati for utterly, then say \emph{sampūrṇ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{બિલકુલ} (bilkul)}{બિલકુલ (bilkul)}]{\gu{બિલકુલ} (bilkul) — absolutely; at all (with a negative)}

\label{lesson:GU-C379-bilkul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for utterly, then the Gujarati for complete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{બિલકુલ}}
\textbf{\gu{બિલકુલ}} — \emph{bilkul} — \textquotedblleft{}absolutely; at all (with a negative)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તમે} \gu{ઝડપી} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{ચલાવશો} \gu{તો} \gu{હું} \gu{બિલકુલ} \gu{નહીં} \gu{બેસું}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tame jhaḍpī gāḍī calāvśo to hũ bilkul nahī̃ besũ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you drive fast, I absolutely will not get in.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{બિલકુલ}} (\emph{bilkul}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{bil-kull}, \textquotedblleft{}with the whole, entirely\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bilkul}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bilkul}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tame jhaḍpī gāḍī calāvśo to hũ bilkul nahī̃ besũ.} — If you drive fast, I absolutely will not get in.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for utterly, then the Gujarati for complete, then say \emph{bilkul} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{બિલકુલ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Absolutely; at all (with a negative)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{કેવળ} (kevaḷ)}{કેવળ (kevaḷ)}]{\gu{કેવળ} (kevaḷ) — solely}

\label{lesson:GU-C379-keval}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for complete, then the Gujarati for absolutely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{કેવળ}}
\textbf{\gu{કેવળ}} — \emph{kevaḷ} — \textquotedblleft{}solely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{જો} \gu{તમે} \gu{કેવળ} \gu{પૈસા} \gu{માટે} \gu{કામ} \gu{કરશો} \gu{તો} \gu{ખુશ} \gu{નહીં} \gu{રહો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jo tame kevaḷ paisā māṭe kām karśo to khuś nahī̃ raho.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you work only for money, you will not be happy.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{કેવળ}} (\emph{kevaḷ}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{kevala}, \textquotedblleft{}alone, exclusive, entire\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kevaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kevaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jo tame kevaḷ paisā māṭe kām karśo to khuś nahī̃ raho.} — If you work only for money, you will not be happy.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for complete, then the Gujarati for absolutely, then say \emph{kevaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
